chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who designated his slave girl as a hady (sacrificial offering) for the Ka'bah. What should he do? He said: A man came to my father who had designated his slave girl as a hady for the Ka'bah. So he said to him: 'Evaluate the slave girl or sell her. Then instruct a caller to stand upon the Hajar al-Aswad (the Rock) and call out: 'Indeed! Whoever has insufficient funds, or has been cut off (by bandits), or whose food has run out, let him come to so-and-so, son of so-and-so!' And instruct him to give to the first one first until the price of the slave girl is depleted.'

key_terms.الْحِجْرِ: The Hajar al-Aswad (Black Stone) or the area near it in the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: The Ka'bah, the cube-shaped building in Mecca
key_terms.قَوِّمِ: Evaluate or appraise the value of
key_terms.قُطِعَ بِهِ: Cut off, often referring to being stranded or robbed
key_terms.هَدْياً: A sacrificial animal or item offered to God, often during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a slave girl dedicated as a sacrifice for the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of dedicating a female slave as a hady, ruling that she is treated as property to be appraised or sold rather than remaining in servitude. The Imam specifies that the proceeds must be distributed to the needy—specifically those with limited means, severed ties, or depleted food supplies—prioritizing the most urgent cases until the value is exhausted. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the dedication applies to the value or the person's status, ensuring the poor benefit directly from the sacrifice's worth.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Bunan Bin Muhammad, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who made his slave girl to be a gift for the Kabah. What should he do?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man came over to my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> and he had made his slave girl to be a gift to the Kabah. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Evaluate the slave girl, or sell her. Then instruct a caller to stand upon the rock, so he would call out: ‘Indeed! The one who is short with his expenditure, or has been cut-off with (by bandits), or his food is depleted, so let him come to so and so, son of so and so!’ And, instruct him that he should give to the first one first until the price of the slave girl is depleted’.
en.sarwar: 18. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja’far who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who donates his slave-girl to al-Ka‘bah and about how should he deal with it.

He (the Imam) said, ‘Once a man came to my father who had donated his slave-girl to al-Ka‘bah. He (the Imam) told him to find the value of the slave or sell her; then announce near the Black Stone and say, “Those who are short in their expenses, being looted on the way or who have depleted their supplies, can come to so and so.” Instruct him to distribute it on the basis of first come first served until the entire fund is distributed.’”
